lyrics:
[Intro: warm electric guitar arpeggios in six, soft organ]

[Verse 1: gentle soulful male voice]
I learned to tie a tie from a video
Learned to shave from a guy at school
Signed my own permission slips
Got good at making do

Father's Day I'd stay home sick
Never knew what card to buy
Told myself it didn't matter
I'm pretty good at lies

[Chorus: fuller, choir humming, tender]
Then you were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Verse 2: voice close, guitar and bass]
Somebody taught me a prayer one night
Starts with two words: "Our Father"
I got as far as the second one
And couldn't go any farther

'Cause the one who made the mountains
Sent his only boy for me
So a kid with no one in the bleachers
Could be family

[Chorus: fuller, choir humming, tender]
And you were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Bridge: band swells, voice breaking]
Abba. I'm still learning how to say it.
Jesus called you that in a garden, crying
Now he's teaching me. I'm trying.

[Final Chorus: full band and choir, then down to a hush]
You were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Outro: guitar alone, whispered]
Our Father...
